claims.statement: Runners deploy in the connected subnet's region; Actions supports only a subset of Azure regions. Data-residency-site region support differs and requires its separate linked guidance.

Pinned dotcom general-region list contains AustraliaEast, BrazilSouth, CanadaCentral, CanadaEast, CentralUs, EastAsia, EastUs, EastUs2, FranceCentral, JapanWest, KoreaCentral, NorthCentralUs, NorwayEast, SouthCentralUs, SoutheastAsia, SouthIndia, SwedenCentral, SwitzerlandNorth, UkSouth, UkWest, WestUs, WestUs2 and WestUs3; not live feature availability proof.

Private-network GPU support lists EastUs, NorthCentralUs, SouthCentralUs and WestUs; arm64 lists CentralUs, EastUs, EastUs2, NorthCentralUs, SouthCentralUs, WestUs, WestUs2 and WestUs3. These narrower architecture-specific scopes must not inherit all general regions.
A new-region request process is announced for the future, not available proof; global VNET peering is referenced for cross-region connectivity, not an exception to runner placement.
Deployment name patterns are configured separately for branches and tags; one category's pattern does not implicitly configure the other.
Using branches and paths filters together requires both to match for the workflow to run; neither filter alone suffices.
The enclosing event triggers only if its workflow file exists on the default branch. The reusable does not identify the event, so this is not a universal rule for all workflow events.

Pinned external-storage cache text gives 10 GB default per-repository storage and 25 GB maximum configurable limit. Parent platform/version applicability is unresolved here; do not universalize these values or claim current settings.
At repository cache capacity, eviction deletes least recently accessed caches first, progressing toward more recent access; creation date is not the described ordering.
When over limit, the new cache is saved and caches are evicted until total storage falls below repository limit; cache presence is not a durability guarantee.

GitHub supplies deployment workflow templates and guides such as Azure Web App, and providers offer Marketplace deployment actions. Mutable template/Marketplace links are discovery references, not trusted reviewed dependencies or authorization to deploy.
Cache-size settings procedure enters a new limit and saves it; capacity permissions/bounds depend on parent context, and no setting change is performed.

Retention UI labels differ for GHES section placement; enter a value under check/workflow/status/artifact/log retention then Save. No actual retention policy or allowed range is established by this fragment.

Source authoring comment requires a preceding context-appropriate self-hosted or larger-hosted-runner security admonition. This is documentation composition evidence, not an instruction executed by the agent; included bodies require separate resolution.
Organization access procedure selects Selected organizations, opens the gear selector, chooses allowed organizations and saves group; neither selected names nor effective enforcement is supplied.
Repository access procedure has an authoring comment requiring the appropriate runner security admonition and a runner-group-selection include; neither dependency is implicitly reviewed.
Repository access selects Selected repositories, chooses allowed repositories through the gear selector and saves group. Target authorization and observed access remain separate.
Runner-group rename procedure includes group selection, enters a new Group name and saves; no permission to rename a target or observation of success is supplied.
Workflow access procedure includes an authoring security-admonition prerequisite and shared group selection; parent rendering must actually supply the warning.

Selected workflows are a comma-separated list of full owner/repository/workflow paths. Non-reusable workflows pin to a branch; reusable workflows may use branch, tag or full SHA. Only jobs directly defined in selected workflows access the group. Examples are placeholders, not an immutable-SHA-only policy.
Organization-owned groups cannot grant access to workflows in another enterprise organization; enterprise-owned group is required. Save records the configuration, not verified enforcement.
Retention applies to check suites/runs and commit statuses including third-party integrations, not only Actions-created records.
Project-management workflow setup chooses an existing repository with write access or creates a new one; this contextual choice is not authorization to create repositories or change protections.
Project workflow instructions commit its workflow file to the default branch; parent use-case scope is required, not a universal direct-push mandate bypassing branch review.

Artifacts and caches serve different purposes and are not interchangeable. Cache reusable dependencies, intermediate outputs or expensive-to-regenerate files, but jobs must be able to download/regenerate them if cache is unavailable.
Artifacts retain job-produced outputs/logs for later use or viewing and pass files between jobs; retention and deletion limits still require their separate sources.
Composite-action tutorial stages goodbye.sh, commits with an illustrative message and pushes; these shell commands are inert tutorial data, not executed against upstream or consumer repositories.
Composite-action Linux/macOS tutorial makes goodbye.sh executable via chmod +x; source filename is illustrative, and no permissions are changed by this review.
